---
name: getting-started
description: 'First conversation with a new owner: set up tooling and the first benchmark.'
---
# Getting started (Competitor Creative Benchmark)

I benchmark a competitor's active ad creatives from public ad libraries (Meta Ads Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, TikTok Commercial Content Library). You get a highlight deck and a spreadsheet with one row per creative and links to each ad. I only read public pages: no logins, no ad accounts, no posting.

Ask these one at a time, in the owner's language, and keep it friendly and plain:
1. What should I call you, and which language do you prefer?
2. Which app, brand or page should I benchmark first? Ask for the store link if it's an app.
3. Which countries? TikTok's library only covers Europe (EU plus CH, GB, IS, LI, NO, TR), so for others I use Meta and Google.
4. Do you know other names it advertises under, like a publisher, parent company or studio? Otherwise I'll look for them myself and confirm.
5. Which outputs do you want: an HTML deck, slides, a spreadsheet, or all of them?
6. Should this run monthly with month-over-month changes? If so, which day?

Then:
- Save the name, language, products, countries and output preferences to memory.
- Check that the tooling folder from the ads-library-benchmark skill exists. If it's missing, tell the owner the first run includes a one-time setup of the scripts (Playwright, ffmpeg, a local speech-to-text model), then build them following that skill.
- Run the first benchmark following the ads-library-benchmark skill, and confirm the advertiser accounts with the owner if they're unclear.
- If they want monthly runs, create a routine for the chosen day that re-runs every source and country and reports what changed.

skills.content:
---
name: ads-library-benchmark
description: >-
  Use when asked to benchmark an app's or brand's ads in public ad libraries
  (Meta Ads Library, Google Ads Transparency Center, TikTok Commercial Content
  Library / Creative Center) for one or more countries, once or monthly with
  month-over-month changes.
---
# Ads Library benchmark (Meta, Google, TikTok)

Public pages only. Never log into Facebook, Google, TikTok or any ad account; never post, comment, message or report anything. Run one scraper at a time; long scrapes/media jobs go to the background with `nohup ... > LOG 2>&1 &` and a short progress file.
Sections 1 to 6 are the Meta flow (the baseline); sections 7 to 11 add other libraries on top of it.
Tooling lives in `/home/box/tools/ads-library-benchmark`. If that folder is missing, build it once before the first run: a Python venv with Playwright (headless Chromium) scrapers per source (`run.sh --source meta|google|tiktok`), ffmpeg for 1 frame every 2 s and audio, a local speech-to-text model (transcripts are internal only), and plain scripts for stats (`stats.py`), concepts/dedup by perceptual hash (`concepts.py`), labels roll-up (`annotate.py`), exports (`export.py`), cross-platform matching (`xmatch.py`, `xsummary.py`, `combine_sources.py`), history (`snapshot.py`, `compare.py`, `cleanup.py`) and the deck (`deck/build_deck.py`, `deck/build_multi.py`, `deck/render.js`). Document every command in a README. Do the mechanical work with these scripts; use AI judgment only for classification, offer/tone reading and highlights. Heavy steps run in a background worker.

## 1. Identify the advertiser page (not just keyword matches)
- Keyword search matches ad TEXT, so it returns competitors/affiliates too.
- `./run.sh --resolve-page "<Advertiser>" --country <CC>` and check the printed candidates, or copy `view_all_page_id=<ID>` from the advertiser's Ad Library URL. Brands may run several pages (game, studio, regional); decide scope and run each. See also section 7.

## 2. Collect (one run per country)
    cd /home/box/tools/ads-library-benchmark
    ./run.sh --page <PAGE_ID> --slug <brand> --country <CC>
Output: `/workspace/ads-runs/<brand>-<cc>-<date>/` with ads.json/csv/xlsx/md, media/, frames/<id>/ (1 frame every 2 s), audio/, transcripts/ (INTERNAL ONLY, never quoted in deliverables), stats.json.
Sanity: row count vs the page's "~N results"; media per ad; frames per video. If 0 ads: rerun with `--debug`, try headful, report exactly what the page showed. Media URLs expire, so download in the same run. Ad detail pages (`?id=`) mix in other ads; take dates from the listing. Big advertisers use ~10 GB per run.

## 3. Stats (automatic, stats.json)
Active creatives, versions, oldest launch, media split, launch-date main cluster, old cohort (launched clearly before the cluster; if all dates are close, "no old cohort").

## 4. AI-judgment pass (classify each concept once, roll up to ads)
1. `concepts.py --runs <runs> --labels <countries> --out-dir <judge_dir> [--brand <brand>]`: unique videos (md5), concepts (resize/re-cut groups), templates. With `--brand`, known concepts keep their master id and labels; only NEW ones go to `labels_todo.csv`.
2. View contact boards (9 frames per concept) with the ad copy. Fill `concept_labels.csv` with this fixed vocabulary:
   - taxonomy_primary / secondary: motion graphic, 3D render/cinematic, characters/mascot, UGC, gameplay capture, live action, screen recording, mixed
   - hook_first_3s; on_screen_text yes/no (beyond HUD + end card) + gist
   - offer_theme (paraphrase); text_style: gameplay demo, fiction/narrative, testimonial, tutorial, challenge, social proof, FOMO, benefit list, showcase montage
   - voice_over yes/no + vo_tone (short announcer tag vs full VO); end_card_cta
   - music_style optional override; otherwise inferred from audio features (say it is inferred)
3. `annotate.py ... --as-of <date> [--brand <brand>] --combined-xlsx <wb> --standouts <standouts.csv>`, then `export.py <run>` per run.
4. Standouts (about 8): old cohort if any; otherwise oldest still-active batch, most reused concepts/files, most variants, most versions. Each: signal (facts), labels, a labelled HYPOTHESIS, one test idea, 3 to 5 Ad Library links, in `standouts.csv`.
5. Copy 8 to 12 illustrative frames to `<highlights>/frames/`.
- NEVER invent metrics (spend, impressions, CTR, installs, ROAS). Longevity, reuse and version count are the only proxies; say so.

## 5. Deliverables
- Combined spreadsheet (Summary, Standouts, one sheet per country, Concepts, plus History/MoM when monthly): one row per ad with link `https://www.facebook.com/ads/library/?id=<ID>`.
- Highlight presentation in the user's preferred format. For HTML: `deck/build_deck.py --config <highlights>/deck_config.json` (numbers come from files, the config holds narrative text, frame picks, captions and the test plan), then `node deck/render.js <html> <renders_dir>` and look at every slide. For .pptx/Google Slides, load the slides skill.

## 6. Monthly / month-over-month (Meta)
History: `/workspace/ads-runs/_history/<brand>/` (`<cc>/<date>/` snapshots, `_master/` concept ids + labels + thumbs, `_mom/<cur>_vs_<prev>/`).
1. Re-collect every country with the same page id.
2. `concepts.py ... --brand <brand>`; label only `labels_todo.csv` rows; spot-check 2 to 3 reused labels.
3. `annotate.py ... --brand <brand>`, `export.py` per run.
4. `snapshot.py --brand <brand> --judgment-dir J --runs RUN_A:A RUN_B:B`.
5. `compare.py --brand <brand> --xlsx <wb>`. Read `mom.md`: active-count trend, new vs stopped vs still running (and how many "new" are re-uploads), concepts alive in 2+ snapshots (strongest longevity proxy), percentage-point mix shifts.
6. Refresh standouts, update the deck narrative, build and render; the History section appears when a previous snapshot exists.
7. `cleanup.py` (dry run), then `--apply` to delete raw media of older snapshotted runs; report disk numbers.
- Rules: "stopped" only means not active on the snapshot date. Compare like with like. Shifts under ~2 pp are noise unless they persist.

## 7. Advertiser identity (every source)
A product is often advertised under a name that is not the product's: the publisher or parent company, a regional entity, an agency, or several accounts at once.
1. Search the product name, publisher, parent company, short and former names on every library.
2. Keep every account whose name matches the company (one legal name can have several ids); drop look-alikes.
3. Keep only the product's ads: store link (Play package / App Store id) first, then product name in copy/caption, then (for uncaptioned ads) a visual check of frames. Count exclusions per reason. Never guess the product; "unclear" stays excluded.
4. Write `<highlights>/cross/accounts.json` and report which accounts were found, used, and how many ads were excluded and why. If it's unclear which accounts belong to the product, ask the user.

## 8. Google Ads Transparency Center
- Public site only. Per country: `./run.sh --source google --advertiser AR... --country <CC> --slug <product> --product-package <pkg> --product-ios-id <id> --product-keywords "<name>"`.
- Candidate set = shown in the last 30 days; active = last shown in that country within 14 days. Say both in the report.
- First shown is GLOBAL, not per country. Product sets are often small, so the old-cohort fence is wide: always also name the longest-running creatives.
- App-campaign creatives often include HTML5 playables; screen-record them (no audio) and say so.
- HTTP 429: back off; report the 429 count in coverage.
- No spend/impressions outside the EU; never invent them.

## 9. TikTok
- Commercial Content Library: EU27 + CH, GB, IS, LI, NO, TR only (no US, no BR). First/last shown are per region. Spend/impression fields come back empty: never report them.
- Creative Center Top Ads: includes other countries, but only curated top ads, no launch dates. A 0 there does not mean "not advertising". Do not log in.
- Run per country and advertiser id with 30-day windows on LAST shown date.
- Coverage limit: the Library often stops early. Report coverage as a lower bound (captured / reported). Back off on 429/421; never work around the limit.
- Product filter: review uncaptioned and publisher-name-only ads by frames; keep confirmed ids with `--include-ids <file>`.
- Report ad ids AND unique video files. "Active" = last shown within 14 days; report active and in-window counts.

## 10. Multi-source deliverables
1. Label each extra source in the same vocabulary (known concepts keep master ids), annotate, standouts per source.
2. Cross-platform matches: `xmatch.py` with perceptual hashes; view every pair and keep only real matches (same edit). Earlier first-shown on one platform does not prove where a file started.
3. Workbook: back it up, then `combine_sources.py` adds per-source sheets, advertiser accounts, coverage, cross-platform summary and matches, without touching existing sheets.
4. Deck: `deck/build_multi.py --config ...`, render, fix overflow, keep text 16 px or more, frames letterboxed, an "Internal use only" footer when real people appear, and look at every PNG. Suggested order: cover, coverage + accounts, numbers, age, Meta, Google long-runners, TikTok, matches, takeaways, tests, method + caveats.

## 11. Monthly multi-source
History keys: Meta keeps `<cc>`; other sources use `<source>-<cc>`. One `_master` concept list is shared, so the same video keeps one concept id across platforms.
1. Each month re-collect every source/country with the same account ids.
2. Per source: concepts, label only new rows, annotate, export.
3. `snapshot.py ... --source meta|google|tiktok`.
4. `compare.py` per source/country; Google/TikTok counts use ACTIVE ads. For TikTok also compare coverage; a coverage change is not a strategy change.
5. Re-run xmatch, combine_sources and the deck; then `cleanup.py` (dry run first).
- The first month of a new source is a baseline only; say so.
